@graph.comment: Private backend, reachable only through a runtime-owned IPC socket. The outer loopback gateway authenticates every read and write. Private content is encrypted by the Interego publisher; this backend does not encrypt arbitrary plaintext resources. Notifications and federation transports are not enabled by this profile.

comment: The internal value storage reads /.internal/ from the file backend, not through the full ResourceStore.
CSS 7.3 lists a container there by running `for await` over the container's body. Through the full store
that body is Turtle, in which it finds no member, inside the locking store's wrapper, which `for await`
cannot read: the hourly expired-entry sweep waited out the 6 s resource lock and crashed the process,
about an hour after every start. The backend answers with the quads themselves, as it does for CSS's own
urn:solid-server:default:BackendKeyValueStorage. What this gives up is the resource lock on the documents
this storage owns (accounts, cookies, OIDC and setup entries). Besides CSS's own setup at boot and the
sweeps, only CSS's account and OIDC routes write those, and the gateway forwards only requests under the
pod's own path, so it never reaches them. If it ever forwards them, this storage needs the lock back.
The resource locker's reader counts stay in memory, beside the in-memory locker that uses them, as
css:config/storage/key-value/memory.json keeps them; this storage holds nothing else. On the file backend
every pod read wrote and then deleted a count under /.internal/locks/. The sweep walks all of /.internal/,
and a count is a bare number with no key, so a sweep that ran while a read was open threw and deleted nothing.
